question: Though the Nature Restoration Regulation set 1 September 2026 as the deadline for Member States to submit their draft national restoration plans (NRPs), only eight countries have done so to date. Upon receiving an NRP, the Commission has six months to provide an assessment and feedback, after which the Member State in question has another six months to submit its final plan. In view of the above: 1.
When does the Commission expect to receive the remaining 19 draft NRPs, and what information has it received from the Member States in question?
What action is the Commission taking with regard to the Member States that have failed to meet this deadline?
How will the Commission ensure that these delays do not adversely affect the Regulation’s implementation timeline or compromise its targets for 2030?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.11.2026) By 27 October 2026, nine Member States had submitted their drafts. According to the Commission’s information, technical preparations are well advanced, or completed, in several others and are at the stage of political validation. The Commission is in contact with all Member States and they are all actively progressing in this work.

By letter of 11 September 2026, the Commission reminded Member States of the importance of submitting their draft plans as soon as possible. It underlined that national restoration plans are the main implementation tool under the Nature Restoration Regulation1 and are essential for translating its targets into action at national level.

It also highlighted the link between national restoration plans and future programming under the next multiannual financial framework2. The Commission has engaged, and continues to engage, with Member States on this matter, through continued dialogue, including capitals visits and meetings of DirectorsGeneral for Environment and of the Nature Restoration Expert Group3.

Moreover, at the Environment Council of 12 October 2026, the Commission urged Member States to speed up the submission of still pending drafts. Many restoration measures are already underway, and Member States do not need to wait for the finalisation of their national restoration plans to make progress on the ground.
The priority now for the Commission – with the support of the European Environment Agency4 – is to help Member States deliver robust final plans, through a constructive assessment process.
1 Regulation (EU) 2024/1991 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 24 June 2024 on nature

restoration and amending Regulation (EU) 2022/869, OJ L, 2024/1991, 29.7.2024. 2 https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/eu-budget/long-term-eu-budget/eu-budget-2028-2034_en. 3 https://ec.europa.eu/transparency/expert-groups-register/screen/expertgroups/consult?lang=en&fromMainGroup=true&groupID=104912. 4 https://www.eea.europa.eu/en.
